personal-bot is an independent, third-party interoperability project. "QQ", "Tencent" and related marks belong to their respective owners. Nothing here is provided, reviewed or approved by Tencent.

What it does, plainly ​

The stack runs the official, unmodified QQ NT desktop client for Linux inside a container, on a virtual display, and does three things with that client:

  • it reads messages out of a private, decrypted copy of the client's own local database, which never leaves your machine;
  • it sends messages by calling the client's own send function through a small library the container preloads into the client at launch - no file of the client is patched, replaced or written to;
  • it clicks the client's own 登录 button over the accessibility bus when the client returns to its account page, so a saved session resumes on its own. A QR login stays manual, and it is yours to do.

It reads nothing else. It does not read your contacts beyond the names the client itself shows, it does not listen to any event stream of the client, and it sends nothing anywhere except the model provider you configure and the MCP servers you connect.

The risk is yours ​

Automating a chat client is outside that client's terms of service. The account you run this with can be restricted, suspended or permanently lost, and your local message history can be lost with it. That risk is yours, and you take it on voluntarily.

To keep it as small as it can be:

  • use a secondary account that already has some history, not a fresh one;
  • run on a residential connection, not a datacenter IP;
  • keep the default send pacing, and do not raise it;
  • keep the client's own version, and do not let it update itself.
